claim: A Duke wall wearing door art (CheckDoorTile, e.g. DOORTILE23) with a lotag is a Use control like a switch: using it operates the activators and master switches on that lotag and plays its hitag as a sound. A converter that treats only switch tiles as controls loses these senders, leaving their receivers with nothing to start them.
evidence: reference/eduke32/source/duke3d/src/sector.cpp:3590-3593 (P_CheckSectors: a used wall with lotag > 0 and door art goes to P_ActivateSwitch), :1351-1352 (P_ActivateSwitch lets a door tile pass) and :1519-1533 (G_OperateActivators, G_OperateMasterSwitches(lotag), hitag played as a sound)
E4L1 wall 2318 (maps/duke3d/E4L1.MAP: picnum 4391, lotag 8000, hitag 327): its three charges and three falling sectors were converted on two channels with no sender
use: List tagged door-art walls as controls when converting (conversion_coverage reports them as tagged_use_wall) and wire them by hand until the converter lowers them.

checked.how: eduke32 sector.cpp read: :148-174 CheckDoorTile lists DOORTILE1..23 (DOORTILE23 = 4391, names.h:664); P_ActivateSwitch (:1266) returns 0 for a wall of lotag 0 (:1294-1295), :1351-1352 default case passes a door tile; :1519-1521 G_OperateActivators, G_OperateForceFields, G_OperateMasterSwitches(lotag); :1526-1533 plays hitag as a sound. P_CheckSectors :3590-3593 calls it for a used wall with lotag > 0 and door art. Duke maps/duke3d/E4L1.MAP wall 2318 (read_duke_map): picnum 4391, lotag 8000, hitag 327.
